A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same flow-attention and FlowDAGNN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the expanded and reorganized Appendix G.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original PowerGraph classification and Ckt-Bench101 regression experiments in Tables 1–2, plus training and inference measurements in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those original experiments and adds attention-weight correlations, Graph Transformer comparisons, and citation-network and molecular-graph evaluations in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Outgoing-neighbor attention normalization and the reverse/forward FlowDAGNN procedure remain unchanged in Sections 5.1–5.3. GT/FlowGT become TransformerConv/FlowTC through terminology clarification, without a new algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 adds node classification on Cora, CiteSeer, and PubMed and molecular graph classification on ogbg-molhiv. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained power-grid classification and circuit-regression tasks to different domains and node-level prediction.

E2.justification: Appendix G.2 and Table 5 add SAT, GraphGPS (GPS in the table), and Exphormer to the PowerGraph comparisons, substantially broadening the comparator families. SAT-based DAGformer already appeared in the circuit experiment, whose comparator set is retained. GT becoming TC is only a rename.

E3.justification: The existing experiments retain their splits, optimizers, training budgets, and model-selection settings. Added experiments specify three-layer, 32-dimensional Graph Transformers and public splits with Optuna TPE validation for the non-flow benchmarks, using accuracy or ROC-AUC and sum pooling for molecular graph readout.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.1 and Figure 6 compare learned attention weights through correlation matrices on all four PowerGraph systems, probing differences between standard and flow attention. This is a focused diagnostic addition. The existing efficiency analysis moves from Appendix G to G.4.

E5.justification: The five-seed PowerGraph and ten-seed circuit results retain their mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and efficiency measurements retain ten-run averaging. Added tables continue repeated-seed averaging and plus/minus reporting; no increased run counts for existing experiments or new uncertainty-testing procedure are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical numerical results after matching renamed models. New Figure 6 and Tables 5–6 add substantial results: Graph Transformer PowerGraph scores, attention correlations, and mixed non-flow outcomes. For example, Table 6 reports Cora accuracy of 81.2% for GAT versus 80.3% for FlowGAT, but ogbg-molhiv ROC-AUC of 74.9% versus 75.9%. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, expressivity results, Theorem 5.4, and Appendix A proofs are substantively retained. Lemma 5.2 explicitly says outgoing neighborhoods match in both multisets, clarifying a condition already stated and used in v1's proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: conservation-inspired attention, greater expressivity, FlowDAGNN, and improved performance over standard-attention counterparts on flow graphs. Proposed future integration into Graph Transformers does not change the present contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 adds substantive applicability boundaries: broadcasting and equivalent informational graphs may disadvantage flow attention, while repeated features may make it useful for molecules. Appendix G adds explanations of attention correlations and frames stronger Graph Transformer results as an accuracy–computational-cost tradeoff.

D1.justification: The added experiments document Transformer layer counts and hidden dimensions, public data splits, Optuna TPE selection, and molecular sum-pooling/MLP readout. Existing implementation settings, V100 hardware disclosure, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Graph Transformer comparisons, non-flow benchmarks, and hyperparameter optimization. It clarifies TransformerConv's relationship to UniMP and global-attention models and discusses flow attention as a possible local component within Graph Transformers. The original related-work argument and novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained with language corrections. Section 4 is renamed, Section 5.4 is added, and Appendix G gains subsections while retaining efficiency analysis. Author/header text and reference ordering also change.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR typography, title and author formatting, headers, and extensive text/float reflow. It adds the correlation heatmaps and Tables 5–6. Existing efficiency Figures 6–7 become Figures 7–8 and are reformatted side by side; the earlier core illustrations and tables remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the stronger comparator coverage and non-flow tests provide better evidence about competitiveness and applicability, including unfavorable outcomes. Reporting weaknesses temper the gain: Appendix G.2 overstates uniform Transformer superiority, which Tables 1 and 5 do not support for Exphormer on IEEE118, and the claimed computational tradeoff lacks timings for the new comparators.
